name: InvestiNator — DataOps Incident Investigation
stack: Python · FastAPI · Next.js · PostgreSQL · Kafka · OpenAI (optional)
problem: Platform incidents scatter evidence across services, slowing the path from a symptom to an auditable recovery decision.
solution: Correlate telemetry and incident context, investigate with read-only tools, require approval, and verify recovery against evidence.
flow: Local Kafka producer / consumer + simulated ReplayLab fault signals
FastAPI telemetry → threshold rules → topology correlation
PostgreSQL incident, evidence, approval and audit state → Next.js operator UI
Read-only tools → optional configured OpenAI Responses; model output cannot authorize writes
Policy / approval → allowlisted simulated recovery → metric verification
context: Data platform operators need to distinguish upstream causes from downstream symptoms. The public Pages UI uses synthetic scenarios, while the local Compose stack provides the API-backed workflow. Neither is a deployed enterprise monitoring service.
challenges: Correlated alerts do not prove causality. Telemetry provenance, event time, tenant boundaries and explicit uncertainty must survive the investigation. A real local Kafka workload must not be confused with the injected disk-pressure scenario.
decisions: The architecture documents separate evidence retrieval from model reasoning and action policy. PostgreSQL makes incident and approval state persistent; FastAPI exposes the workflow and Next.js presents it. These are observable implementation choices, not evidence of an exhaustive vendor comparison. A rule-only workflow is a useful alternative baseline for stable incidents.
implementation: The reviewed main branch includes the Python/FastAPI default backend, SQLAlchemy/Alembic persistence, local Kafka workload, replay scenarios, read-only investigation tools and optional OpenAI integration. A Java foundation exists, but the README flags later operator/security work on feature/java-ai-audit as unmerged; do not present that branch roadmap as the main deployment. Public chat is offline by default and can use a separately configured gateway.
security: The documented action executor is limited to a simulated allowlisted recovery. Demo identity is not production OIDC/RBAC. Redaction and evidence-ID validation are implemented boundaries; they do not establish production tenant isolation or a security certification. Public preview has no production connectors or infrastructure write authority.
value: Expected value: reduce evidence-gathering friction and make incident decisions reviewable. No measured reduction in incident investigation time, outage loss or operational cost is claimed. Offline workflow tests measure demo behavior, not enterprise RCA accuracy.
future: Validate production identity and isolation; evaluate connector freshness and failure handling; benchmark supported-diagnosis time against a human/rule baseline; review the separate Java branch and release gates before any production cutover.

name: VerdaTrace — Governed Cloud Data Platform
status: Implemented reference platform; cloud deployment not verified
stack: Python · Pub/Sub · GKE · BigQuery · GCS · Terraform
problem: Heterogeneous datasets are difficult to use safely when quality, ownership, provenance and suitability are disconnected.
solution: Ingest and profile data through a shared pipeline that publishes normalized results, quality findings, lineage and explainable visualization recommendations.
flow: Registered local / attributed sample datasets → bounded ingestion
Quality checks → catalog / semantics → analysis → task-suitability evaluation
Normalized results + lineage / governance → generated frontend portal payload
Cloud worker path: Pub/Sub → GKE Python worker → BigQuery curated tables + controlled GCS archive
Cross-cutting IAM / Workload Identity / secret redaction / audit / monitoring
context: Analysts and platform teams need to know whether data is appropriate for a task, not merely whether a file loaded. The repository includes a real attributed weather sample and explicitly synthetic mobility/quality fixtures. Its cloud infrastructure definition is distinct from local processing and static visualization.
challenges: Parsing multiple formats introduces resource and path risks. Dataset semantics can be uncertain; a recommendation should preserve source evidence and warnings. Large external raster/OSM inputs and cloud execution have dependencies beyond the included local fixtures.
decisions: The shared normalized-result contract separates analysis from presentation, allowing the portal to consume pipeline outputs rather than disconnected numbers. The versioned registry makes onboarding explicit. Terraform and Kubernetes describe the cloud path; they do not prove a successful cloud apply. A simpler single-format pipeline could cost less where multimodal extensibility is unnecessary.
implementation: Verdatrace modules implement ingestion, registry validation, quality, cataloging, analytics, evaluation, lineage and visualization decisions. scripts/build_demo.py builds frontend/data/platform_demo.json. main.tf, deployment.yaml and data_pipeline.py define the Pub/Sub worker and GCP resources. Some candidate datasets are disabled retrieval plans, not committed operational datasets.
security: Code and configuration include allowed path roots, allowlisted HTTPS retrieval, role checks, redaction, scoped IAM, workload identity and raw-storage public-access prevention. These controls require deployment validation. Optional raster workers and external data packs remain separate execution boundaries.
value: Expected value: make quality and provenance visible before analytics consumes data and reduce repeated dataset assessment work. The case study claims no cloud cost savings, quality uplift percentage or production throughput. Local fixture tests are correctness evidence only.
future: Exercise the cloud deployment in an authorized test project, validate IAM and retention behavior, test representative larger datasets, and benchmark query/use-case readiness before claiming scale or savings.

name: DataGuard-AI — Telecom Reliability Monitoring
status: Seeded monitoring MVP; not production SaaS
stack: Python · HTTP API · JavaScript · Rule-based monitoring
problem: Missing feeds, late batches and revenue variance can leave telecom teams acting on incomplete information.
solution: Classify feed and ETL health, generate owned alerts, and show transparent estimated revenue exposure beside operational evidence.
flow: Seed feed, job and revenue records + fixed scenario clock
Rule-based classification / runtime thresholds / historical revenue baseline
Alerts + estimated impact in process memory
Python ThreadingHTTPServer JSON routes → static dashboard
Owners and recommended next checks accompany alerts; no implemented ML/LLM layer
context: The target users are telecom data engineering and revenue-assurance teams. A clear alert owner and expected file arrival time make an issue actionable. The reviewed MVP demonstrates this interaction with seeded data, not a live billing feed.
challenges: An estimate of exposure is not booked revenue loss. Late and missing feeds require different reasoning, and incident duplication can inflate totals. Static scenario time makes the demo deterministic but cannot serve as continuous production monitoring.
decisions: The actual API uses Python standard-library ThreadingHTTPServer and dataclasses, not FastAPI despite the CV technology label. monitoring.py contains explicit rules rather than an AI model. This keeps the demo inspectable. A durable API framework, scheduler and database are future options, not implemented architecture.
implementation: api.py creates seeded feed/job/metric lists at import, maps GET endpoints, serializes dashboard objects and serves web/. monitoring.py evaluates arrival deadlines, runtime deviations and revenue baselines. The impact calculation prorates and caps an average daily revenue input; alert IDs are generated in memory.
security: No authenticated multi-tenant production service, durable alert lifecycle, live ingestion connector or resilient scheduler is established by the reviewed code. Treat the API as a local MVP. A production design needs identity, persistence, deduplication, audit, retention and freshness checks.
value: Expected value: prioritize feed investigation and make assumptions about exposure visible. All revenue-at-risk values shown by the MVP are scenario-based estimates, not measured revenue saved. No reduced leakage or availability KPI is asserted.
future: Add durable event/alert storage, replace the fixed seed clock with controlled ingestion, validate impact estimates with revenue owners, and evaluate authentication and duplicate-alert behavior before any SaaS claim.

name: Banking Fraud Detection Pipeline
stack: Kafka · Spark Streaming · HDFS · HBase · NiFi · Power BI
problem: Explore how suspicious transaction signals can move from streaming ingestion to analyst-facing outputs.
solution: A repository combines synthetic ATM events, streaming model-inference code, storage artifacts and dashboard evidence.
flow: Synthetic ATM producer → Kafka (legacy ZooKeeper deployment documented)
Spark Streaming / model references → HDFS bronze / silver
Documented NiFi transfer → HBase → Power BI artifacts
Connector configs, model files and complete runtime need validation
context: This is an educational fraud-pipeline architecture, not a certified banking decision system. Synthetic transaction generation supports exploration without implying real customer deployment.
challenges: The streaming script references spark and configuration classes without defining them in that file. Its legacy pyspark.streaming.kafka API and model paths require a compatible runtime and artifacts. Container files and screenshots alone cannot prove end-to-end execution.
decisions: The repository uses Kafka for event transport and separate storage/serving layers. The trade-off is a large operational surface for a learning project. A smaller stream-to-table baseline would be an alternative to evaluate, not an alternative known to have been evaluated by the author.
implementation: Kafka producer files, a streaming script, a silver notebook, HBase DDL, NiFi screenshots and a Power BI file are present. README architecture and actual configuration must be reconciled before running; no successful integrated run is claimed.
security: Validate model/data lineage, replay correctness, offset handling, least-privilege access and false-positive cost before using any fraud output operationally. The README uses a legacy ZooKeeper design; this is not presented as a new KRaft deployment.
value: Expected educational value: understand the ingestion-to-serving chain. Fraud detection accuracy, latency, throughput and avoided losses are unmeasured in this review.
future: Create reproducible dependencies and model fixtures, resolve runtime/configuration gaps, add integration tests and evaluate model error costs on an appropriately governed dataset.

name: Airflow Employee Dimension ETL
status: Code-backed learning pipeline; external services not run
problem: Keep changing employee attributes available for historical reporting rather than overwriting prior values.
solution: An hourly DAG extracts HR/finance data to S3, identifies changes and branches into Snowflake dimension updates and inserts.
flow: PostgreSQL HR / finance → SqlToS3Operator → S3 CSV extracts
Python change detection → Airflow branching / XCom
Snowflake update / insert tasks → historical employee dimension
context: Historical dimensions help analysts interpret a result using the attributes that applied at the relevant time. The repository demonstrates the orchestration pattern with named external connections.
challenges: SCD Type 2 requires consistent effective dates, unique current rows and safe reruns. Branching reduces empty-operation failures but does not establish transactional correctness under retries. Provider versions and credentials are external prerequisites.
decisions: The code uses Airflow tasks to make extraction, change detection and load dependencies explicit, with S3 as a staging boundary. For a smaller workflow, a database-native scheduled job might be simpler. The repository does not record an evaluated alternatives study.
implementation: Dags/ETL_DAG.py uses PostgreSQL/S3 connection IDs, a Python change-detection helper and Snowflake operators. Includes contains SQL and transformation functions. Output screenshots are present. README retains template setup instructions and upstream image attribution; present as a learning project, not sole invention of the pattern.
security: Connection configuration, secrets, retry-safe writes and least-privilege data access must be validated against real services. No live PostgreSQL/S3/Snowflake test was executed here.
value: Expected value: consistent historical reporting and inspectable workflow dependencies. No reduction in processing time or operational cost is claimed.
future: Pin supported Airflow/provider versions, replace template setup instructions, add deterministic SCD fixtures and test reruns/partial failures before a production claim.

name: Databricks Customer Sales Analysis
problem: Explore customer value, geographic revenue concentration and purchase recency in a controlled sales dataset.
solution: SQL cohorts, country totals, recency flags and a dashboard turn synthetic customer records into inspectable analytical outputs.
flow: 100 synthetic customer records (repository documentation)
Databricks SQL cohort / revenue / recency queries
Dashboard screenshot → analytical interpretation
context: The dataset is synthetic and cannot demonstrate actual customer retention or revenue improvement. Recency flags are indicators, not validated churn predictions.
challenges: Analytical definitions and date cutoffs must be explicit. A segment threshold that works in a fixture does not establish a business intervention policy.
decisions: SQL keeps grouping and ranking logic inspectable; a CSV fixture bounds the exercise. No production ingestion or real-time serving architecture is established.
implementation: The repository includes customer_sales_summary_small.csv, SQL Queries and Customer_Sales_Dashboard.png. Workspace execution and dashboard publication were not rerun in this task.
security: The synthetic dataset avoids using real customer information. Production adaptation would need access controls, data contracts and validation of revenue definitions.
value: Demonstrated artifact scope is customer segmentation and revenue/recency analysis, not improved customer lifetime value. No financial uplift is reported.
future: Add query-level assertions, versioned date cutoffs, source-to-total reconciliation and reproducible workspace instructions.
